pre-commit.description: Renovate's pre-commit manager is opt-in. Without this the hook revisions in .pre-commit-config.yaml are the one dependency file nobody is watching -- and those hooks are the linters gating every commit, so the thing judging everything else goes unjudged.

customManagers.description: Pick up the shellcheck-py pin in tox.ini's [testenv:shellcheck] deps. Renovate has no tox manager, so without this the pin is invisible to it -- and enabling the pre-commit manager above would then bump the hook alone, leaving CI (which runs the tox environment) and developers (who run the hook) disagreeing about what passes. The shellcheck group below lands both in one pull request.

Pick up the skillsaw pin in functional-tests.yml's sanity_checks job. The linter is installed into the test venv rather than run as stbenjam/skillsaw@v0, whose composite action pins actions/setup-python to a version with no Debian 12 build, so Renovate's github-actions manager never sees it. Without this the pre-commit manager would bump the hook alone, leaving CI and developers disagreeing about what passes. The skillsaw group below lands both in one pull request.

packageRules.description: Flag minor, patch, and digest updates for review (not auto-merged)

Group the two shellcheck pins together. The pre-commit hook revision and the tox.ini dependency must move as one: .pre-commit-config.yaml says to keep them in lockstep, and nothing enforces it if they arrive in separate pull requests. The two names differ because they come from different datasources -- a GitHub tag for the hook, a PyPI release for the tox pin.

Tell Renovate how to read shellcheck-py's four-component tags. Upstream tags a fourth component -- v0.11.0.1 is shellcheck 0.11.0, packaging revision 1 -- which is not semver, so the github-tags datasource behind the pre-commit hook could not even resolve the current value and reported "Can't find version matching v0.10.0.1" on the dependency dashboard. The lookup failing meant the hook never got an update proposed, which silently defeated the shellcheck group above: this pull request initially carried the tox pin alone, and CI would have linted with a newer shellcheck than the hook developers run. The PyPI side needs none of this because pep440 handles four components natively. The fourth group is deliberately named build rather than revision even though it is a packaging revision: Renovate's regex versioning only appends revision to the comparison array when a build group matched too, so naming it revision would truncate every tag to three components and make v0.11.0.2 compare equal to v0.11.0.1 -- a packaging-only release, which is most of them, would never be proposed. The regex is anchored to exactly four numeric components so that v0.11.0.1-1, a re-tag with no matching PyPI release, is ignored rather than proposed as an upgrade that would break the lockstep from the other direction.

Group the two skillsaw pins together, for the same reason as shellcheck above. The pre-commit hook revision and the CI install must move as one: .pre-commit-config.yaml says to keep them in lockstep, and nothing enforces it if they arrive in separate pull requests. The two names differ because they come from different datasources -- a GitHub tag for the hook, a PyPI release for the CI pin.

pydantic exact-pins its matching pydantic-core release, so it must never be updated independently -- doing so always breaks dependency resolution (see PR #198). pyproject.toml deliberately carries no pydantic-core pin; this rule stops Renovate proposing one or bumping a stray pin if one ever reappears.

Group the protobuf / gRPC ecosystem together. grpcio-tools pins protobuf to a compatible major, and the checked-in stubs in kerbside/rpc/ must be regenerated (tox -egenprotos) whenever protobuf moves, so these must bump as a coordinated set.

Group the Rust tonic / prost ecosystem together. The generated gRPC stubs in rust/kerbside-proxy/ are produced at build time by tonic-prost-build and consumed by tonic + tonic-prost, so a runtime crate that moves without its code generator produces stubs that will not compile (see the tonic 0.14 breakage: tonic and prost went to 0.14 while tonic-build stayed on 0.12, and the emitted code still named the removed tonic::codec::ProstCodec). These must bump as a coordinated set.
